hook.line: After a long night at the café, Vale asks if you were exhausted. There are two honest answers: you fell asleep, or you were not tired enough to.
hook.es: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
hook.en: I was so tired I fell asleep.

examples.es: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
examples.en: I was so tired I fell asleep.

examples.es: No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.
examples.en: I wasn't tired enough to fall asleep.

examples.es: Hace tanto frío que no salgo.
examples.en: It's so cold that I'm not going out.

examples.es: No hace tanto frío como para no salir.
examples.en: It isn't cold enough to stay in.

examples.es: Es tan caro que no lo compro.

examples.es: No es tan caro como para no comprarlo.
examples.en: It isn't expensive enough to not buy it.

rule:
Spanish has two ways to say "so… that".
*Tan… que* + a normal verb reports something that really happened: *Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.* I did fall asleep.
*Tan… como para* + an infinitive gives a threshold, "enough to": *No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.* It does not say it happened. It is usually negative.
Quick test: if the result is a fact, use *que*. If it is only a measure of enough, use *como para*.
Before a noun like *frío*, use *tanto*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *que* here a result clause and *como para* a clause of degree or purpose.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *que* or *como para*, then type the whole sentence: Estaba tan cansado ___ me dormí. (I was so tired I fell asleep.)
yourTurn.answer: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
yourTurn.why: I really did fall asleep, and a real fact with its own verb takes *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *que* or *como para*, then type the whole sentence: No estaba tan cansado ___ dormirme. (I wasn't tired enough to fall asleep.)
yourTurn.answer: No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.
yourTurn.why: It is a measure of "enough" followed by an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It's so cold that I'm not going out.
yourTurn.answer: Hace tanto frío que no salgo.
yourTurn.why: A real result, so *que* + a normal verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It isn't cold enough to stay in.
yourTurn.answer: No hace tanto frío como para no salir.
yourTurn.why: A threshold with an infinitive, so *como para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It's so expensive that I don't buy it.
yourTurn.answer: Es tan caro que no lo compro.
yourTurn.why: The result is a fact, so it takes *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the fact into a threshold: *Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.* becomes: I wasn't tired enough to fall asleep.
yourTurn.answer: No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.
yourTurn.why: Make it negative, swap *que* for *como para*, and use the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *El problema es tan grave como para cerrar.* becomes: The problem isn't serious enough to close.
yourTurn.answer: El problema no es tan grave como para cerrar.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes before the verb; *como para* stays.

pitfalls.wrong: Estaba tan cansado como para me dormí.
pitfalls.right: Estaba tan cansado que me dormí.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A real result with its own verb needs *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: No estaba tan cansado que dormirme.
pitfalls.right: No estaba tan cansado como para dormirme.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For "enough to" with an infinitive, use *como para*, not *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hace tan frío que no salgo.
pitfalls.right: Hace tanto frío que no salgo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Frío* is a noun here, so it takes *tanto*; *tan* goes before adjectives.

personal: Tell me something you were so tired, hungry or busy that you did, with *tan… que…*
